To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the new method of fission in inverse kinematics allows for a precise and complete determination of the isotopic yield distribution of fission fragments, and that the isotopic yield distributions are strongly dependent on the mass of the fissioning system.
1) We measured the isotopic yield distributions from transfer and fusion induced fission in the reaction 238U(12C,Xf) for the first time.

(i) the isotopic yield distributions are strongly dependent on the excitation energy of the fissioning system, (ii) the fragment isotopic yield distributions can be described by a Gaussian distribution in the mass number, and (iii) the isotopic distributions are not affected by the angular momentum of the fission fragments, which can be deduced from the measured fragment emission angles.
